Cleveland heart disease: what this benchmark actually shows

26 July 2026 · UCI Cleveland (1988) · n = 302 patients · prepared for the clinical data-science lead

The answer

This file's celebrated accuracy is an artefact of duplication and label-adjacent features; the real, decision-relevant signal is worth 0.87 AUC, it comes almost entirely from the exercise stress test and symptom presentation, and it must not be deployed.

Executive summary

Situation. The Cleveland heart-disease file is one of the most-benchmarked tabular medical datasets in existence. Published results on it routinely report 95–100% accuracy, and those numbers are cited as evidence that the problem is essentially solved.

Complication. The file does not contain 1,025 patients. It contains 302 patients copied 3.4 times on average, and two of its strongest predictors are produced by the very catheterisation procedure that defines the label. Under the standard protocol a random forest scores a perfect 1.000 AUC — because 99% of its test set has an exact twin in its training set.

Resolution. Deduplicated to 302 patients and restricted to measurements available before the catheter, the honest performance is 0.873 AUC (95% CI 0.833–0.910) — good enough to triage, nowhere near good enough to diagnose. The signal lives in the exercise stress test and symptom presentation; resting cholesterol and fasting blood sugar carry none.

Key line 1

The file is 302 patients, not 1,025 — and the standard protocol inflates accuracy by 18%

723 of 1,025 rows (70%) are exact copies, and two out-of-dictionary codes turn out to be missing data wearing valid-looking numbers. Every benchmark that splits before deduplicating is measuring memory.

Key line 2

11 of 13 measurements separate the groups — and the two that fail are the two a screening programme would have bet on

Exercise-stress response and symptom presentation carry the diagnostic signal. Resting cholesterol and fasting blood sugar do not survive multiple-comparison correction, and that null result is one of the most useful findings here.

Key line 3

Honest performance is 0.873 AUC, angiography-derived features add only +0.038, and one threshold flags 88% of women vs 55% of men

The model is a triage instrument at best. Its subgroup behaviour is unequal in a way a single global threshold cannot fix, and a 1988 single-cohort model with n = 302 is not a deployment candidate.

Recommendation

  1. Mandate dedup-before-split and a declared feature scope for any tabular medical benchmark this group publishes or reviews. Treat existing results on this file — including our own — as void until re-run. The check costs one line of code and is worth 18% of apparent accuracy.
  2. Prioritise the exercise-stress variables — ST depression, exercise-induced angina, ST slope and age-adjusted peak heart rate — in any prospective triage study. Do not build one around resting cholesterol or fasting blood sugar; neither survives correction here.
  3. Do not deploy, and do not fund a deployment pilot on this data. A 1988 single-cohort model with n = 302, no external validation, and a threshold that flags 88% of women versus 55% of men is a methodological artefact, not a clinical instrument.

The famous 100% accuracy is memorisation — deduplication costs 18 accuracy points

Identical model, identical 13 features; only the split changes. The random forest returns a perfect 1.000 AUC on the duplicated file and 0.904 on unseen patients. Ten-fold CV does not rescue it — the folds share the same patients.

So what: treat every published accuracy figure on this file as void unless the paper states it deduplicated first. Mandate dedup-before-split as a review checkpoint; it costs one line of code and it is the difference between 100% and 82%.

Part I · Integrity

The file is 302 patients, not 1,025 — and the standard protocol inflates accuracy by 18%

723 of 1,025 rows (70%) are exact copies, and two out-of-dictionary codes turn out to be missing data wearing valid-looking numbers. Every benchmark that splits before deduplicating is measuring memory.

1,025 rows resolve to 302 patients, replicated 3.4× on average

723 rows (70%) are exact duplicates. The label balance also shifts under deduplication (51.3% → 54.3% positive), so the copying was not uniform.

So what: the effective sample size is 302, and every confidence interval in this report is sized accordingly. Any analysis quoting n = 1,025 is overstating its precision by roughly a factor of √3.4.

The three protocols, side by side

Identical models and identical features throughout; only the split changes. P2 is the protocol usually offered as the rigorous alternative to a single holdout — and it is just as contaminated, because cross-validation protects against an unlucky split, not against duplicated rows.

Two "valid" codes that were missing data

Schema validation at ingestion found 6 patients carrying codes the data dictionary does not permit — thal = 0 and ca = 4 — the original UCI ? markers coerced into numbers. Modelling them as real categories would have invented a thallium result and a fifth coronary vessel. They were recoded to explicit missing values, and a sensitivity check confirms the conclusion is unchanged (+0.0030 AUC when those patients are dropped instead).

Part II · Signal

11 of 13 measurements separate the groups — and the two that fail are the two a screening programme would have bet on

Exercise-stress response and symptom presentation carry the diagnostic signal. Resting cholesterol and fasting blood sugar do not survive multiple-comparison correction, and that null result is one of the most useful findings here.

11 of 13 measurements survive FDR correction — the stress test dominates

Every feature is reported with an effect size and a bootstrap confidence interval, not a p-value alone. Benjamini–Hochberg correction is applied across all 13 tests.

So what: a prospective triage study should capture ST depression, exercise angina, ST slope and age-adjusted peak heart rate first. These are the measurements that carry the information, and they are all obtainable before a catheter.

Resting cholesterol and fasting blood sugar carry no detectable signal in this cohort

Cholesterol differs between groups by 8 mg/dl with a CI spanning zero (-20 to 3); neither feature survives correction.

So what: this is a reported null result, not an omission. In a cohort already referred for angiography, resting lipids add nothing on top of the stress test — so a triage score built on them would be measuring the wrong thing. Note the scope: this is a statement about discrimination within a referral population, not about whether cholesterol causes heart disease.

Under mutual adjustment, chest-pain type and ST depression stay significant — resting clinical status collapses entirely

Scope 1 multivariate logistic regression, pseudo-R² = 0.426, maximum VIF = 1.71 (no collinearity problem).

So what: the univariate ranking survives adjustment, which means the signal is structural rather than an artefact of one test's assumptions. Odds ratios are reported with CIs so a clinician can read the magnitude directly.

Part III · Limits

Honest performance is 0.873 AUC, angiography-derived features add only +0.038, and one threshold flags 88% of women vs 55% of men

The model is a triage instrument at best. Its subgroup behaviour is unequal in a way a single global threshold cannot fix, and a 1988 single-cohort model with n = 302 is not a deployment candidate.

Model choice is irrelevant here; feature scope is what moves the number

Every classifier lands within one standard deviation of every other — the spread across models (0.048 AUC) is smaller than the fold-to-fold noise within any one of them (±0.066). Allowing angiography-derived features in buys only +0.038 AUC.

So what: stop tuning. On this data the return to model complexity is zero and the return to interpretability is high, so regularised logistic regression is the model of record. The flexible models actually finish lower — the same capacity that made contamination so profitable buys only variance once the duplicates are gone.

At a clinically chosen threshold the model catches 148 of 164 disease cases, at a cost of 50 false alarms

The threshold is set for 90% sensitivity because a missed diagnosis is the costly error — 0.5 is never assumed optimal. Specificity at that point is 64%.

So what: stated in patients rather than rates, the trade is explicit: 16 patients with disease still go home undiagnosed, and 50 healthy patients are sent for further workup. That is a defensible triage trade and an indefensible diagnostic one.

Discrimination is comparable across sexes, but one shared threshold flags 88% of women against 55% of men

Female AUC 0.896 (CI 0.803–0.967) vs male 0.836 (CI 0.780–0.889). But specificity is 46% for women against 68% for men, driven by 75% vs 45% referral prevalence.

So what: the model ranks women at least as well as men, so this is not a discrimination failure — it is a threshold-equity failure. Any prospective study must be powered for women specifically (n = 96 here) and must decide deliberately whether it equalises sensitivity, specificity or flag rate, because at these prevalences it cannot equalise all three.

Sex is reconstructible from the remaining clinical features at only AUC 0.599 — barely above chance. Unlike most datasets, dropping the sex column here genuinely would remove most of its direct influence. That makes it a live design option, but it would not touch the prevalence-driven threshold effect, which is the actual problem. The weakest age band is 56-65 (AUC 0.786).

Appendix

Method, evidence and limitations

What was done

Six notebooks, run in order, each gated against the Tier A stage checklist: ingestion and schema validation → cleaning and duplication forensics → exploratory analysis → statistical testing → modelling, evaluation and the fairness audit → this report. All numbers on this page are read from machine-written artefacts; none are typed by hand.

Why a single train/test split is not enough at n = 302

The one-touch held-out test (61 patients) returns AUC 0.826 with a 95% CI of 0.716–0.923 — a band 0.21 AUC points wide, far too wide to rank models. The headline figure is therefore repeated stratified 10-fold cross-validation (50 fits), and hyperparameters are tuned in a nested inner loop: tuning on the reported folds would have printed an optimistic +0.0049 AUC, a smaller cousin of the duplication error this report is about.

Feature engineering — a reported negative result

Six clinically motivated derived features (chronotropic reserve, guideline threshold flags, graded ST severity, a composite risk count) were built and ablation-tested. They moved CV AUC by +0.0012 (logistic) and +0.0028 (random forest) — inside the noise band — and were therefore rejected. The information was already present in the raw measurements. At n = 302 the parsimonious model is also the more trustworthy one.

Model of record

Logistic regression (L2), Scope 1 pre-test features, C = 1.0. Out-of-fold ROC-AUC 0.873 (95% CI 0.833–0.910), PR-AUC 0.888, Brier 0.144 (42% better than always predicting the base rate). Top features by permutation importance: sex, cp, oldpeak, thalach, exang — 4 of 5 agree with the independent Stage 5a effect-size ranking, which is itself evidence that the signal is stable rather than an artefact of one method.

Cohort composition after deduplication — 68% male, ages 29–77.

Numeric distributions by outcome — thalach and oldpeak separate; chol and trestbps overlap.

Categorical disease rates — chest-pain type and ST slope carry the contrast.

Calibration — Brier 0.144, 42% better than the base rate.

Limitations

  • 1988 single-cohort referral population — these are associations among patients already selected for angiography, not population prevalence. The inverted age effect (disease patients are younger on average, 52.6 vs 56.6 years) is a signature of that selection.
  • n = 302 after deduplication. Every confidence interval in this report is wide, and they are reported rather than hidden.
  • No external validation cohort, and no temporal data — so no drift analysis is possible.
  • Causal inference is out of scope by design: every feature is an observed marker or test result, not an assignable intervention. "Lower cholesterol to reduce disease" is not supportable from this data.
  • Not calibrated for, and not intended for, patient-facing deployment.

Reproducibility

RANDOM_STATE = 42 in every notebook; pinned requirements.txt; restart-and-run-all passes end to end from heart.csv alone. The notebooks import no local modules, so a fresh clone runs with nothing but the pinned packages.
